name: Nano Banana 2.1

setting.label: 1K drafts
setting.note: Start with a 1K draft. Set 4:5 for a portrait feed image or 16:9 for a wide banner. Change the aspect ratio to suit the channel.

description: An editorial first choice for trying visual directions and refining a short campaign brief in a conversation.

price.note: Standard Gemini API example. Input, text, thinking, and optional grounding may add charges.

concepts.bestFor: Quick concepts for a campaign, social post, or landing page.
concepts.example: Try three visual directions for a managed-services launch banner.
concepts.limitation: Leave space for approved headlines and add them in your design tool.
concepts.stepUp: Use a more controlled editing workflow when approved product details must stay put.

edits.bestFor: Conversational revisions where several drafts are useful.
edits.example: Explore warmer lighting on an approved campaign reference.
edits.limitation: Inspect each revision for unintended changes to the original.
edits.stepUp: Use a targeted edit workflow when one small area needs to change.

image.brief: Create a wide editorial photo for a managed IT service launch. Show a small team collaborating in a bright office. Leave the left third uncluttered for a headline. Keep the colors neutral and omit any text or logos.

name: Adobe Firefly Image5

setting.label: Speed for drafts
setting.note: In the browser, select Adobe’s own Image5 model where available. The speed and quality reasoner options shown here are Firefly Services API controls.

description: A starting point for teams already working in Adobe, especially for ideation and refinements before final layout.

price.note: Check regional Adobe plans and eligible model credits. A plan allowance does not establish an Image5 API rate.

concepts.bestFor: Campaign concepts in an Adobe-centered design workflow.
concepts.example: Explore a set of neutral office backgrounds for a service brochure.
concepts.limitation: Check which model and credit allowance your plan uses.
concepts.stepUp: Choose a controlled edit when the approved source image must be preserved.

edits.bestFor: Prompt-driven edits to an approved image in an existing Adobe workflow.
edits.example: Replace a distracting background in a brochure photo.
edits.limitation: Inspect the subject edges, original colors, and retouching artifacts.
edits.stepUp: Finish precise edge cleanup in the editor you already use.

image.brief: Use the approved photo as a reference. Replace the background with a warm light-gray studio wall. Keep the subject’s expression, pose, clothing, and lighting unchanged.

name: GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst

setting.label: Medium quality, low edit complexity
setting.note: Start with low complexity for a narrow edit. Raise it only when the brief needs a larger composition change. Use the Image API edits route with an approved reference.

description: An editorial first choice for controlled image edits and detailed visual briefs.

price.note: Image, text, and reference inputs can contribute to the API bill.

edits.bestFor: Targeted edits when you have an approved reference and clear preservation rules.
edits.example: Remove glare from a product photo while keeping ports, label, framing, and colors.
edits.limitation: Compare against the source at full size. A generated edit can change small details.
edits.stepUp: Use a human retouch when the image must show exact product markings or specifications.

layout.bestFor: Detailed compositions with explicit placement and short copy.
layout.example: Mock up a webinar banner with an open area for a single line of text.
layout.limitation: Inspect spelling and spacing, then set final copy as editable text.
layout.stepUp: Build the final deliverable in a layout tool when the text must stay editable.

image.brief: Edit only the background and glare on the supplied product photo. Use a neutral studio backdrop. Keep the product angle, body shape, port count, labels, proportions, and colors. Leave the crop unchanged.

sources.label: GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst model and rates

name: Ideogram 4.6

setting.label: Medium quality, exact copy
setting.note: Select Ideogram 4.6 in the browser where available and check its credit quote. In the API, turn off prompt rewriting when the wording must be exact.

description: An editorial first choice for visual concepts with lettering, such as posters and social cards.

price.note: API rate for medium-quality text-only generation. Check the separate pricing for edits, web credits, and higher resolutions.

layout.bestFor: Artwork where a short headline is part of the composition.
layout.example: Draft an event poster featuring the exact words “Secure by Design”.
layout.limitation: Proofread the image and rebuild final dates, prices, and legal copy as editable text.
layout.stepUp: Use your design tool for exact brand typography and reusable layouts.

concepts.bestFor: Campaign concepts where the relationship between artwork and a short heading matters.
concepts.example: Try different typographic directions for a webinar campaign.
concepts.limitation: Treat wording, kerning, and spacing as draft material.
concepts.stepUp: Move into an editable design file when the idea has been approved.

image.brief: Design a portrait event-poster concept with the exact headline “Secure by Design”. Use a solid off-white backdrop and one dark red graphic. Leave a clean bottom area for the date and logo. Add no other text.

name: Qwen Image 3.0 Pro

setting.label: 1K concept output
setting.note: Select 1K output in the model settings for the rate shown here. Check the endpoint and price for your region.

description: A hosted Qwen option for exploring multilingual layouts and image concepts.

price.note: International QwenCloud list rate. 2K output and reference images are priced separately.

layout.bestFor: Layout concepts that need short wording in more than one language.
layout.example: Mock up an English and Danish version of an event poster.
layout.limitation: Have a native speaker proof each word and put final copy in an editable layer.
layout.stepUp: Use a layout tool if brand fonts and exact text positions are required.

concepts.bestFor: A second visual direction for a campaign when layout is part of the brief.
concepts.example: Try two arrangements for a service launch card with room for localized copy.
concepts.limitation: Check the regional rate and inputs before planning a batch.
concepts.stepUp: Use a dedicated typography or layout workflow when the copy becomes central.

image.brief: Draft a clean two-column visual for a bilingual IT services event. Leave editable space for English and Danish headlines. Use a neutral office illustration on the right and avoid logos, small text, or invented details.

name: FLUX 3 Image

setting.label: 1K output with references
setting.note: Use the flux-3-image endpoint. Check the output size limits for reference-based edits. Use approved input images.

description: A useful alternative for combining approved references into a single campaign composition.

price.note: BFL’s published 1K generation or editing rate. Higher resolutions cost more.

edits.bestFor: Composition changes that combine several visual references.
edits.example: Place an approved device image into a new office scene for a campaign mockup.
edits.limitation: Inspect the result for modified hardware, logos, and product proportions.
edits.stepUp: Keep the original product photography in the final layout when accuracy matters.

image.brief: Compose the approved product photo and office reference into a portrait campaign concept. Keep the product proportions and port layout. Use a simple desk scene and leave clean space above it for copy.

sources.label: FLUX 3 Image endpoint and supported settings

name: Qwen-Image-2512

setting.label: 50-step generation example
setting.note: These are example settings from the model card. Your team must set up and verify a local deployment first.

description: A downloadable text-to-image model for locally generated concepts once a compatible deployment is configured.

price.note: No measured cost for the team’s hardware.

concepts.bestFor: Local image concepts on a team-managed deployment.
concepts.example: Create an abstract background for an internal campaign draft.
concepts.limitation: This entry covers text-to-image generation. Verify your hardware and runtime first.
concepts.stepUp: Choose a configured edit-specific model if you need to preserve an existing photo.

layout.bestFor: Local drafts exploring where text and artwork could sit.
layout.example: Sketch a two-line heading above an illustration for an internal event.
layout.limitation: Rebuild the approved wording in an editable layer and check the result.
layout.stepUp: Use a design tool to finalize brand fonts and spacing.

image.brief: Generate a simple, wide background for an internal IT awareness presentation. Use muted neutral colors, a sparse abstract network pattern, and open space for an editable heading. Do not include text.
